t: Compulsory third party motor insurance was first introduced in India through which legislation?
e: Chapter VIII of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 made third party insurance compulsory in India (brought into force from 1 July 1946). The 1988 Act replaced it and continues the requirement in Chapter XI.

t: Which of the following describes the role of the Tariff Advisory Committee (TAC) in motor insurance before 2007?
o: It fixed premium rates, terms and policy wordings through the India Motor Tariff
It settled third party claims on behalf of insurers
It licensed surveyors for motor claims
It operated the hit-and-run compensation scheme
e: The TAC, a statutory body under the Insurance Act, controlled rates, terms and wordings through the India Motor Tariff until pricing was de-tariffed on 1 January 2007. Policy wordings continued to be standardised even after de-tariffing.

t: From which date was pricing of motor own damage insurance in India de-tariffed?
e: IRDAI withdrew tariff control over premium rates for motor own damage (and other non-life classes) with effect from 1 January 2007. Third party premium rates, however, continued to be regulated.

t: The Indian Motor Third Party Insurance Pool (IMTPIP) was created in April 2007 mainly to:
o: Share own damage losses of private cars among all insurers
Share the third party liability business of commercial vehicles among all non-life insurers
Reinsure motor risks with GIC Re only
e: The IMTPIP pooled commercial vehicle third party (Act only) business so that every insurer shared the losses in proportion to its overall market share. It operated from April 2007 and was replaced by the Declined Risk Pool from April 2012.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which of the following is correct?
o: No person shall use a motor vehicle in a public place unless a policy covering third party risks is in force
Insurance is compulsory only for commercial vehicles
Insurance is compulsory only against damage to the vehicle itself
Insurance is compulsory only for vehicles above 1500 cc
e: Section 146 makes it an offence to use, or allow another to use, a motor vehicle in a public place without a policy that complies with Chapter XI (third party risks). Own damage cover is optional.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 came into force (for most provisions) on:
e: Most provisions of the 2019 Amendment Act, including enhanced penalties and the new no-fault compensation section, were notified with effect from 1 September 2019.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), the no-fault compensation payable in case of death of a victim is:
e: Section 164 provides ₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous hurt without the claimant having to prove negligence. It replaced the earlier Section 140 (₹50,000 / ₹25,000) and Section 163A.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: A Motor Accident Claims Tribunal is constituted by the State Government under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988?
e: Section 165 empowers State Governments to constitute one or more Claims Tribunals to adjudicate compensation claims arising from motor accidents. Section 166 deals with the application for compensation and Section 173 with appeals.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Which of the following is NOT excluded from the definition of 'motor vehicle' under Section 2(28) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988?
o: A vehicle running upon fixed rails
A vehicle of a special type adapted for use only in a factory or enclosed premises
A vehicle with less than four wheels and engine capacity not exceeding 25 cc
A tractor used on public roads
e: Section 2(28) excludes rail-borne vehicles, special vehicles used only in factories/enclosed premises, and vehicles of fewer than four wheels with engine capacity up to 25 cc. Tractors are motor vehicles and need Act cover when used in a public place.

t: Under the depreciation schedule for partial losses, metal parts of a vehicle aged between 1 and 2 years attract depreciation of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The age-based schedule for 'all other parts' is: up to 6 months nil; 6 months–1 year 5%; 1–2 years 10%; 2–3 years 15%; 3–4 years 25%; 4–5 years 35%; 5–10 years 40%; above 10 years 50%.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 157 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, when a vehicle is sold, the transferee must apply to the insurer for necessary changes in the certificate of insurance within:
e: Section 157 deems the certificate and policy transferred to the new owner along with the vehicle, and requires the transferee to apply to the insurer within 14 days for the changes to be made in the certificate and policy.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, an application for compensation under Section 166 must ordinarily be made within what period from the date of accident?
e: The 2019 amendment re-introduced a limitation of six months for filing a claim under Section 166(3). Before this, the limitation clause had been deleted in 1994 and claims could be filed at any time.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: For private car insurance, the 'limitations as to use' clause permits the vehicle to be used for:
o: Carrying passengers for hire or reward
Social, domestic, pleasure and professional purposes, including the insured's own business
e: Private car policies allow use for social, domestic, pleasure and professional purposes and for the insured's business, but exclude hire or reward, carriage of goods (other than samples), racing, pace-making, speed testing and motor trade use.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Which of the following vehicles would be classified as a 'Miscellaneous and Special Type' commercial vehicle for motor insurance purposes?
o: A tempo carrying goods for hire
A motor cab plying as a taxi
e: Miscellaneous and special type vehicles include cranes, mobile rigs, forklifts, tractors, road rollers and similar. Buses and taxis are passenger carrying vehicles, and tempos carrying goods for hire are goods carrying vehicles.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a 'motor cab' is a vehicle constructed or adapted to carry, excluding the driver:
e: Section 2(25) defines a motor cab as carrying not more than six passengers excluding the driver, for hire or reward. A maxi cab carries 7 to 12 passengers excluding the driver.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Following the Supreme Court direction of 2018, a new two-wheeler sold in India must be insured for third party liability for a minimum period of:
e: From 1 September 2018 insurers must issue long-term third party cover of 5 years for new two-wheelers and 3 years for new private cars, as directed by the Supreme Court and implemented by IRDAI.

t: An insured cancels his annual package policy after 7 months at his own request. The OD premium of ₹24,000 is refunded to the extent of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). On cancellation at the insured's request the insurer retains premium on short period scale, which is 80% for a period of 7 months. Refund = 20% of ₹24,000 = ₹4,800; had the insurer cancelled, pro-rata refund of 5/12 would apply.

t: As per the IDV depreciation schedule, a vehicle aged more than 2 years but not more than 3 years attracts depreciation of:
e: The schedule is: up to 6 months 5%; 6 months to 1 year 15%; 1 to 2 years 20%; 2 to 3 years 30%; 3 to 4 years 40%; 4 to 5 years 50%. Beyond 5 years IDV is fixed by mutual agreement.

t: The maximum No Claim Bonus (NCB) allowed on own damage premium in India is:
e: NCB progresses as 20%, 25%, 35%, 45% and 50% for successive claim-free years, with 50% being the maximum. It is a discount on the own damage premium only and not on the third party premium.

t: An insured renews a private car package policy 60 days after its expiry without any claim in the expiring policy. What happens to the NCB?
o: NCB is forfeited because the policy lapsed
NCB is retained since renewal is within 90 days of expiry
NCB is halved as a penalty
NCB continues only if the insurer waives the break
e: NCB earned on an expiring policy is protected if the policy is renewed within 90 days of expiry. Renewal beyond 90 days results in loss of the accumulated NCB.

t: The compulsory deductible under a private car package policy for a car with cubic capacity exceeding 1500 cc is:
e: Compulsory deductibles for private cars are ₹1,000 for cars up to 1500 cc and ₹2,000 for cars exceeding 1500 cc. Two-wheelers carry a compulsory deductible of ₹100.

t: A private car has an ex-showroom price of ₹9,00,000 and is 18 months old at the time of insurance. What is the IDV?
e: At 18 months the vehicle falls in the 'exceeding 1 year but not exceeding 2 years' band, attracting 20% depreciation. IDV = ₹9,00,000 less 20% = ₹7,20,000.

t: The discount on own damage premium allowed for an ARAI-approved anti-theft device is:
e: Vehicles fitted with anti-theft devices approved by the Automotive Research Association of India qualify for a 2.5% discount on OD premium subject to a maximum of ₹500 per vehicle.

t: Under the Insurance Act, 1938, Section 64VB requires that:
o: Every motor policy must be issued in Form B
No risk is assumed unless the premium is received in advance
Every claim above ₹50,000 must be surveyed
Policies must be renewed only through agents
e: Section 64VB lays down the 'no premium, no risk' principle: an insurer cannot assume risk unless the premium is received in advance or guaranteed in the manner prescribed. This is why a cover note cannot be issued without premium.

t: A motor cover note issued in India is valid for a maximum period of:
e: Under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules a cover note is valid for 60 days from the date of issue, and the insurer must issue the policy and certificate of insurance within that period.

t: Which of the following is a standard exclusion under Section I (Own Damage) of the private car package policy?
o: Damage while in transit by rail
Consequential loss, depreciation, wear and tear and mechanical breakdown
e: Section I covers named perils such as flood, malicious acts and transit by road or rail, but specifically excludes consequential loss, depreciation, wear and tear, and mechanical or electrical breakdowns, failures or breakages.

t: The standard private car package policy covers reasonable cost of towing a damaged vehicle to the nearest repairer up to:
e: The policy pays reasonable cost of protection, removal to the nearest repairer and re-delivery, limited to ₹1,500 for private cars (₹300 for two-wheelers and ₹2,500 for commercial vehicles) unless enhanced by endorsement.

t: Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017, a complaint can be made to the Ombudsman within what period from the date of the insurer's final reply or rejection?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The complainant must first write to the insurer; if there is no reply within 30 days or the reply is unsatisfactory, a complaint can be lodged with the Ombudsman within one year, provided the matter is not pending before any court or consumer forum.

t: An insured cancels his annual private car package policy after it has run for 4 months. The insurer will retain premium as per short period scale at:
e: Short period scales retain 20% for up to 1 month, 30% for 2 months, 40% for 3 months, 50% for 4 months, 60% for 5 months, 70% for 6 months, 80% for 7 months, 90% for 8 months and full premium beyond 8 months.

t: In a partial loss own damage claim, the depreciation applied on rubber, nylon, plastic parts, tyres, tubes, batteries and airbags is:
e: The policy schedule prescribes 50% depreciation on rubber/nylon/plastic parts, tyres, tubes, batteries and airbags, 30% on fibre glass components, nil on glass, and age-based rates on all other parts.

t: A damaged car is 7 years old. Metal parts replaced cost ₹40,000. What is the depreciation deducted on these parts under the standard schedule?
e: For all other parts (including metal), depreciation for vehicles exceeding 5 years but not exceeding 10 years is 40%. 40% of ₹40,000 = ₹16,000, so ₹24,000 is payable for the parts.

t: A vehicle is treated as a Constructive Total Loss (CTL) when the aggregate cost of retrieval and repair exceeds what percentage of the IDV?
e: The policy defines CTL as a situation where the aggregate cost of retrieval and/or repair of the vehicle, subject to the policy terms, exceeds 75% of the IDV. The claim is then settled on total loss basis.

t: As per the IRDAI Master Circular on General Insurance Business (2024), the insurer must appoint a surveyor within what time of receiving the claim intimation?
e: The 2024 master circular tightened timelines: surveyor appointment within 24 hours, survey report within 15 days, and claim decision within 7 days of receipt of the survey report. Earlier norms under the 2017 regulations allowed 72 hours and 30 days respectively.

t: Non-disclosure of a material fact by the proposer makes the contract:
o: Voidable at the option of the insurer
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Breach of utmost good faith renders the contract voidable, not void; the insurer may elect to avoid it (subject to Section 45 for life).

t: Under the IRDAI Surveyors and Loss Assessors Regulations, a licensed surveyor's report is mandatory for a motor claim where the estimated loss exceeds:
e: The 2015 regulations fixed ₹50,000 for motor claims and ₹1 lakh for other classes as the threshold above which a licensed surveyor must be appointed. Below these limits the insurer may assess in-house.

t: Rahul's car (IDV ₹5,00,000) is a total loss. He opts to retain the wreck, valued at ₹60,000. The compulsory deductible is ₹1,000. What is the claim payable?
e: On a total loss the insurer pays the IDV; if the insured retains the salvage, its value is deducted, and the compulsory deductible applies: ₹5,00,000 − ₹60,000 − ₹1,000 = ₹4,39,000.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under the Indian motor package policy, the limit of liability for third party property damage for a private car is:
e: Third party death or bodily injury liability is unlimited as required by the Act, while property damage liability is limited to ₹7.5 lakh for private cars and commercial vehicles and ₹1 lakh for two-wheelers.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under the Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 2022, the compensation payable for death is:
e: The 2022 Scheme under Section 161 provides ₹2 lakh for death and ₹50,000 for grievous hurt, replacing the earlier Solatium Scheme amounts of ₹25,000 and ₹12,500.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: An appeal against an award of a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal lies to the High Court under Section 173 within:
e: Section 173 allows appeal to the High Court within 90 days of the award. No appeal lies if the amount in dispute is less than ₹1 lakh, and the appellant must deposit ₹25,000 or 50% of the award, whichever is less.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: In Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009), the Supreme Court standardised the multiplier method. For a deceased aged 32 years, the applicable multiplier is:
e: Sarla Verma fixes multipliers by age band: 18 up to 25 years, 17 for 26–30, 16 for 31–35, 15 for 36–40, 14 for 41–45, 13 for 46–50, 11 for 51–55, 9 for 56–60, 7 for 61–65 and 5 above 65.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: In New India Assurance v. Asha Rani (2003), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Gratuitous passengers in a goods vehicle are not covered under an Act policy
Pillion riders are always covered as third parties
Owners of goods carried in a goods vehicle are not covered
The insurer must pay unlimited property damage
e: The Court held that under the 1988 Act an Act-only policy on a goods carriage does not cover gratuitous passengers (persons other than the owner of goods or his representative) carried in the vehicle.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Which of the following is a statutory defence available to an insurer under Section 150(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (earlier Section 149(2))?
o: The vehicle was driven by a person not duly licensed
e: The insurer can contest on limited statutory grounds: breach of a specified policy condition (use for a non-permitted purpose, driver not duly licensed or disqualified, or the vehicle being used in breach of the permit), or that the policy is void for non-disclosure or misrepresentation.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, an application for compensation may be filed with the Claims Tribunal having jurisdiction over the area:
o: Only where the insurer's registered office is located
Only where the vehicle is registered
Where the accident occurred, where the claimant resides or carries on business, or where the defendant resides
e: Section 166(2) gives the claimant the choice of the Tribunal of the area where the accident occurred, where the claimant resides or carries on business, or where the defendant resides.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: A 'Return to Invoice' add-on cover pays, in the event of total loss or theft:
o: The difference between the IDV and the original invoice price of the vehicle (including registration and road tax, as per terms)
The outstanding loan EMIs for six months
e: Return to Invoice bridges the gap between the claim payable on IDV basis and the original purchase price, usually including registration charges and road tax, so the insured can replace the vehicle with a new one.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: Under the 'Nil Depreciation' (zero dep) add-on, which of the following is correct?
o: Depreciation on replaced parts is not deducted from the own damage claim
The insurer waives the compulsory deductible
The IDV is frozen at the invoice value for five years
Consumables such as oils and nuts are always covered
e: Nil depreciation removes the deduction for depreciation on replaced parts; the compulsory deductible still applies and consumables require a separate add-on. Insurers usually restrict the number of claims per year.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: The IRDAI Motor Insurance Service Provider (MISP) guidelines, 2017 relate to:
o: Recognition of automobile dealers as a distribution channel for motor insurance
Pricing of motor third party premium
e: The MISP guidelines brought automobile dealers who solicit motor insurance under IRDAI regulation, requiring sponsorship by an insurer or intermediary and capping the distribution fee payable to them.

t: Deduction for life insurance premium under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act is available up to an overall limit of:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹1,50,000 aggregate for all 80C items; premium qualifies only up to 10% of the sum assured for policies issued after 1 April 2012.

t: The monetary limit of a complaint that can be entertained by the Insurance Ombudsman is:
e: The Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (amended 2021) raised the limit from ₹30 lakh to ₹50 lakh. The complainant must first approach the insurer and may approach the Ombudsman within one year of the insurer's rejection or non-reply.

t: Which of the following is an indicator of a 'staged accident' fraud in motor insurance?
o: A policy renewed on time for ten consecutive years
Policy taken shortly before the accident with inconsistent accident narrative and no independent witnesses
The claimant chooses a network garage
The vehicle has a valid fitness certificate
e: Red flags include proposals or renewals just before a loss, inconsistent or rehearsed statements, absence of independent witnesses, and repeated involvement of the same parties or garages.

t: The database maintained by the Insurance Information Bureau of India (IIBI) helps insurers primarily to:
o: Identify uninsured vehicles and check claim history/fraud across insurers
e: IIBI collects transaction-level motor policy and claims data from all insurers, enabling verification of NCB, detection of multiple claims and identification of uninsured vehicles when linked with the VAHAN database.
